items.title: Design operator roles, console shell and authorization-aware sitemap
items.outcome: Every operator role has a complete task-based console and unauthorized capabilities are structurally absent, while time-boxed grants remain visibly distinct from standing role.
items.context: Admin navigation is an authorization result. A generic sidebar with disabled links can reveal capabilities and normalize access the product is designed not to provide.
scope: Operator personas, base roles, eligibility and temporary grants
My Queue home, status strip and elevation banner
Role-aware sitemap and Tier 0 structural, Tier 1 role and Tier 2 grant absence
Keyboard, screen-reader, density, responsive and performance behavior
acceptance_criteria: Every route lists authorized roles and direct navigation for an unauthorized role fails without revealing content
No route or search provides a browse-all transaction, balance or salary surface
Standing role, approver eligibility and temporary elevation are shown as separate state
Session expiry/revocation preserves no protected view and offers a safe recovery
T-ADM-04 receives a complete D6 shell handoff
contracts_schema: Maps T-CON-07 operator session, role, policy, masked representation and route IDs
security_privacy: Default absence and redaction precede convenience
No financial values or credentials in navigation, analytics or artifacts
observability: Unauthorized route, session expiry, queue discovery and role-confusion signals without customer content
tests: Session revoke and direct-URL attack review
rollout_rollback: D6 shell handoff precedes T-ADM-04 Ready
A missing role mapping removes the route rather than showing a permissive default
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo docs and admin shell page. Admin Design owns route templates; capability squads contribute only authorized destinations.
definition_of_done: Roles/routes/states registered
Authorization and accessibility tests pass
Admin Design, Security, Accessibility and CDO approvals recorded
D6 handoff published and dependencies mirrored

items.title: Design redaction, unmask, elevation, bulk export and break-glass flows
items.outcome: High-risk operator access is deliberately frictive, provenance-bound, four-eyes approved, time-boxed, auditable and fail-closed in every designed state.
items.context: These actions are the console's most dangerous. A generic confirmation or approver dropdown cannot enforce provenance, separation, audit ordering and unavailable-approver behavior.
scope: Eligible ticket/incident/statutory basis verification and ineligible provenance
Break-glass dual-presence, recording, credential rotation and post-use review
acceptance_criteria: Requestor and access-basis originator cannot appear as approver and self-approval is structurally impossible
Closed, invalid, operator-originated, unreachable and audit-write-failed states deny distinctly
No eligible approver produces escalation, never a bypass
Active elevation shows scope and TTL globally and expiry revokes mid-task
T-ADM-03 and T-ADM-05 receive exact D6 handoffs
contracts_schema: Maps T-CON-07 access basis, redaction, elevation, approval, export, expiry and audit states
security_privacy: No key material or unmasked value in prototype examples
User notification and subject-visible event are part of success
observability: Request, denial class, approval age, expiry, early revoke and break-glass outcome without accessed values
rollout_rollback: D6 precedes high-risk admin implementation Ready
Disabling a control disables the protected action and leaves values masked
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo docs. Redaction/elevation, export and break-glass sections have separate owners and one Security approval boundary.
definition_of_done: All access/approval screens and denial states registered
Abuse, accessibility and fail-closed evidence accepted
Security, Privacy and CDO approvals recorded
D6 handoffs published and dependencies mirrored

items.title: Design operator lifecycle, role changes and qualification recertification
items.outcome: Joiner, mover, leaver, approver qualification and recertification tasks expose diffs, conflicts, expiry and safe failure before administrator lifecycle implementation.
items.context: Role changes can silently accumulate privilege. The interface must show removed and added capabilities and prevent self-approval or expired qualification.
scope: Leaver immediate revoke and active-session impact
Qualification matrix, review, expiry, recertification and absence
acceptance_criteria: Every role change shows exact added and removed capabilities before commit
The subject cannot approve their own joiner/mover/recertification
Expired qualification removes approval eligibility and updates active queues
Leaver flow shows session, token and pending approval revocation
T-ADM-06 receives a complete D6 handoff
contracts_schema: Maps operator lifecycle, role diff, qualification, expiry and recertification states
security_privacy: Roster exposes minimum professional data and no customer data
Offboarded identity becomes absent rather than disabled-with-access
observability: Lifecycle completion, self-approval block, recertification age and orphan approval
rollout_rollback: D6 precedes T-ADM-06 Ready
Rollback restores prior role only through a new approved mover action
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo docs. Roster, lifecycle and qualification sections are isolated but share one role/absence model.
definition_of_done: All lifecycle screens/states registered
Security and accessibility tests pass
Admin Design and CDO approvals recorded
D6 handoff published and dependencies mirrored

items.title: Design plans, features, quotas and immutable version operations
items.outcome: Billing managers can create, compare, publish, grandfather and retire immutable plan versions with impact and policy visibility and no edit-in-place affordance.
items.context: A mutable plan editor would silently reprice or re-entitle users. The design must make version creation and subscriber migration the only path.
scope: Before/after impact, affected cohorts and effective date
Retire, conflict, provider-price drift and audit receipt
acceptance_criteria: Published version fields are read-only and edit action creates a new version
Impact preview shows what changes, who is affected and when without exposing individuals
Migration requires notice/effective policy and clearly preserves grandfathered users
Missing/expired jurisdiction or channel policy prevents publish
T-ADM-07 receives a complete D6 handoff
contracts_schema: Maps T-BIL-10 plan version, entitlement, quota, migration, notice and policy states
security_privacy: No per-user financial data in impact previews
High-impact changes require confirmation diff and immutable audit
observability: Draft abandonment, version publish, migration, policy denial and reconciliation drift
tests: Keyboard table and policy fail-closed walkthrough
rollout_rollback: D6 precedes T-ADM-07 Ready
Rollback stops migration and keeps pinned versions
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo docs. Plan catalog, version builder and migration sections use separate branches over immutable-version components.
definition_of_done: All plan/version screens and states registered
Comprehension, policy and accessibility evidence accepted
Billing, Compliance and CDO approvals recorded
D6 handoff published and dependencies mirrored

items.title: Design AI provider, routing, spend-cap and kill-switch operations
items.outcome: AI operators manage approved provider/model/region/retention evidence, routes, spend caps and kill switches without ever viewing secrets or creating an unsafe fallback.
items.context: Provider enablement is default-deny and evidence expires. A conventional settings form could expose keys, omit cap behavior or silently route to an unapproved model.
scope: Kill switch, confirmation, audit and recovery
acceptance_criteria: No raw or masked provider/BYOK key appears anywhere
Provider cannot enable without current region, DPA, retention, model/feature and cost evidence
Cap behavior is mandatory before save and unsafe fallback is impossible
Kill switch is independent, confirmed, audited and immediately visible
T-ADM-08 receives a complete D6 handoff
contracts_schema: Maps provider evidence, model allowlist, route, spend cap, breach behavior and kill-switch states
security_privacy: Secret references only and no user prompt/content
Expired evidence disables routing rather than warning-only
observability: Enable/disable, evidence expiry, cap denial, route health and kill-switch outcome
rollout_rollback: D6 precedes T-ADM-08 Ready
Rollback disables provider/route and never restores expired approval
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo docs. Registry, routing/cap and kill-switch sections are independent branches with one Security/AI Ops review.
definition_of_done: All provider/spend screens and states registered
Security, cost and accessibility tests pass
AI Ops and CDO approvals recorded
D6 handoff published and dependencies mirrored

items.title: Design support, account status, refunds and billing operations
items.outcome: Support operators can resolve account, subscription and refund cases through redacted, provenance-bound and reversible workflows without browsing financial records.
items.context: Support is where convenience pressure can bypass privacy. Common questions should resolve from status and provider evidence before an access request exists.
scope: Case detail/thread/redacted attachment and diagnostic fields
acceptance_criteria: A common billing case resolves without unmasking financial data
Account lookup reveals status only and unavailable/unknown is non-enumerating
Suspend/restore shows before/after, reason, user effect and audit receipt
Refund states map to original charge, entitlement/quota unwind and idempotent provider outcome
T-ADM-09 receives a complete D6 handoff
contracts_schema: Maps T-CON-11 support and T-BIL lifecycle/refund/channel states with narrow ticket verification
security_privacy: Attachments and diagnostics are redacted/allowlisted
Access request uses T-UXM-02 and cannot be self-authorized
observability: SLA risk, resolution without access, refund outcome and escalation without case content
rollout_rollback: D6 precedes T-ADM-09 Ready
Unavailable verification denies access and leaves case status usable
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo docs. Case, account-status and billing-action sections use separate branches over redaction and status components.
definition_of_done: All support/billing operator screens/states registered
Privacy, money and accessibility evidence accepted
Support, Security and CDO approvals recorded
D6 handoff published and dependencies mirrored

items.title: Design the rights-request and grievance operator queue
items.outcome: Rights and grievance officers can prioritize clocks, verify scope, perform bounded actions, record refusal and prove completion without accessing unrelated financial content.
items.context: A request clock without an operator workflow is a compliance failure. Time pressure must not normalize unmasking, silent pause or free-text refusal.
scope: Queue ordered by remaining clock and breach risk
Request detail, verification, jurisdiction profile and evidence references
Enumerated refusal, escalation, assignment and handoff
Verified completion, notification, audit and failed/partial states
acceptance_criteria: Clock source, remaining time, paused/not-paused policy and breach escalation are explicit
Operator sees only data required for the request and high-risk access uses T-UXM-02
Refusal uses an approved code and explanation, never unbounded justification
Erasure/export completion displays evidence and residue/partial failure honestly
T-ADM-13 receives a complete D6 handoff
contracts_schema: Maps T-CON-09 rights, status, clock, refusal, evidence and completion states
security_privacy: No unrelated financial data or operator-created access basis
Statutory profile absence fails closed and escalates
observability: Queue age, breach risk, action outcome, refusal and evidence completion without request content
rollout_rollback: D6 precedes T-ADM-13 Ready
Rollback disables new transitions and escalates open clocks
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo docs. Queue, action and evidence sections are separate branches with one Compliance/Privacy review.
definition_of_done: All rights/grievance screens/states registered
Clock, privacy and accessibility evidence accepted
Compliance, Privacy and CDO approvals recorded
D6 handoff published and dependencies mirrored

items.title: Design audit, access monitoring and aggregate analytics surfaces
items.outcome: Auditors and analysts can verify immutable actions, investigate anomalies and use cohort metrics without editing history, excluding themselves or reconstructing a person.
items.context: Audit and analytics are dense data products with opposite privacy rules: exact action provenance versus aggregate suppression. Generic tables can blur those boundaries.
scope: Anomaly feed, block and on-call escalation
Aggregate cohort dashboards, suppression, narrowing, export and no-data
acceptance_criteria: Audit records are visually and interactively immutable and viewing is itself indicated as audited
Chain verification distinguishes valid, running, failed and break-detected with actionable escalation
Analyst filters accept no user identifier and suppression is distinct from zero/no-data
Two permitted aggregate views cannot be combined through offered controls to isolate a person
T-ADM-10 and T-ADM-11 receive exact D6 handoffs
contracts_schema: Maps T-ADM-02 audit chain, anomaly, cohort minimum, suppression and export states
security_privacy: No copied unmasked value in audit or analytics
Suppression and rate-limit controls are visible and not bypassable
observability: Verification, anomaly review, suppression and attempted narrowing without financial/user detail
rollout_rollback: D6 precedes mapped implementation Ready
Analytics export remains disabled if suppression parity fails
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo docs. Audit/monitoring and aggregate analytics have separate sections and security review because their disclosure models differ.
definition_of_done: All audit/analytics screens and states registered
Immutability, differencing and accessibility evidence accepted
Security, Data and CDO approvals recorded
D6 handoffs published and dependencies mirrored

items.title: Design production-access broker, restore and access-governance views
items.outcome: Authorized platform approvers can confirm zero standing access and govern temporary database, backup, object-store, KMS and restore sessions through a fail-closed operational view.
items.context: Admin-console controls do not cover direct infrastructure access. The healthy state is an empty standing-access inventory, and unavailable approvers must not become a shortcut.
scope: Standing-access inventory and healthy empty state
Restore/snapshot scrub, barrier and availability gate
acceptance_criteria: Standing human read access is visibly zero and any grant is a critical finding
Requestor cannot approve and fewer than two eligible approvers disables new sessions
Session view shows scope, TTL, audit correlation and early revoke
Restore remains unavailable until scrub, RLS, erasure barrier and access checks pass
T-PLT-05 receives a complete D6 operational handoff
contracts_schema: Maps T-PLT-05 inventory, broker, approval, session, restore-check and subject-event states
security_privacy: No reusable credential or query result displayed
Statement fingerprints and counts only
observability: Standing grant, denial, approval age, session expiry and restore-check outcome
rollout_rollback: D6 precedes operational UI enablement
Rollback denies new sessions and never restores standing access
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo docs. Access inventory, broker and restore sections are separate branches reviewed by Platform Security.
definition_of_done: All access-governance screens/states registered
Fail-closed and accessibility evidence accepted
Platform Security and CDO approvals recorded
D6 handoff published and dependencies mirrored

items.title: Design incident, red-team and release evidence operations
items.outcome: Release and security operators can inspect control coverage, attach privacy-safe evidence and run incident actions without modifying the gate or using production customer data.
items.context: A red-team gate that only reports pass/fail is not reviewable, while an evidence UI can accidentally become a production-data bypass.
scope: Incident severity, owner, clock, action and notification
Read-only release decision and waiver/exception state
acceptance_criteria: Operator cannot edit a control result or mark evidence accepted without authorized review
Every failure names reproduction, owner, severity and retest state
Evidence preview rejects raw financial/customer content
Incident clocks and unavailable-owner escalation are explicit
T-ADM-12 and T-QA-13 receive exact D6 handoffs
contracts_schema: Maps security scenario, evidence, finding, retest, incident and release-gate states
security_privacy: Synthetic fixtures only and no production access
Waivers are dated, attributable, expiring and unavailable for prohibited controls
observability: Scenario coverage, evidence expiry, retest age, incident clock and waiver state
rollout_rollback: D6 precedes T-ADM-12/T-QA-13 Ready
Rollback keeps gates closed and evidence readable
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo docs. Red-team/release and incident sections are separate branches over shared evidence/status components.
definition_of_done: All release/incident screens/states registered
Security, privacy and accessibility evidence accepted
Design QA and CDO approvals recorded
D6 handoffs published and dependencies mirrored

items.title: Validate and publish the complete admin operator prototype and handoff
items.outcome: One versioned admin prototype connects every authorized route, queue, approval and incident journey and supplies complete D6 manifests before operator frontend implementation.
items.context: Capability files can pass independently while role absence, queue handoff, elevation banner or audit state fails across the assembled console.
scope: Connected prototypes for every operator role
Happy, deny, unavailable, timeout, expiry, conflict and incident journeys
Dense table, keyboard, screen-reader and performance behavior
Per-ticket D6 manifests, components, contracts, roles and QA scenarios
acceptance_criteria: Every admin registry screen/flow resolves to an immutable frame and D6 artifact
Unauthorized route and direct-link matrices pass for every role fixture
Critical flows pass T-DQA-02, T-DQA-03, T-DQA-06 and T-DQA-08 evidence
No dead link, generic high-risk modal, unmapped component or mutable latest-only handoff exists
T-DQA-12 receives signed Admin Design Lead, Security and CDO readiness
contracts_schema: Publishes admin platform handoff manifest with roles, artifacts, screens/flows, implementation and QA mappings
security_privacy: Synthetic/redacted data only and expiring reviewer access
No prototype route models prohibited browse-all access
observability: Prototype dead links, role leaks, handoff gaps, open high-risk defects and approval age
rollout_rollback: Immutable D6 version precedes mapped admin UI Ready
Material change creates a new version and reopens affected dependencies
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo docs and admin prototype. Platform lead integrates immutable capability branches; feature designers retain defect ownership.
definition_of_done: Complete prototype and D6 manifests published
All required Design QA evidence accepted
Admin Design, Security, Accessibility, UX Engineering and CDO approve
Declared dependencies mirrored as native GitHub blockedBy edges
